title: Pinebay Media - Quickstart credits & hosting evaluation
summary: Discovery call: Pinebay is evaluating Redwood for a PLG quickstart to power an AI assistant for video editing suggestions. Main concerns: time-to-first-token, latency p95, data residency, and pilot economics. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs dedicated vs private, free credits offer, pilot scope, and security controls. Agreed next steps: pilot setup, security docs, pricing, and a benchmarking call.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Latency targets (p95) and cost per 1k tokens
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS & data retention
Pilot scope and success criteria (benchmarks, timeline)
action_items: Aisha: Send pilot credit allocation + quickstart steps (due 2027-06-03)
Diego: Share benchmark template and perf checklist (due 2027-06-04)
Rachel: Provide sample payloads and expected qps for pilot (due 2027-06-07)
next_steps: Start 2-week PLG pilot with 50k token credits
Schedule deep-dive benchmark run with Diego next week
Send security pack (SOC2, ISO, SSO docs) and pricing sheet
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-01 15:00 PT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Aisha Malik (Redwood AE), Diego Fernandez (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (CTO - Pinebay), Ethan Li (Lead Engineer), Sana Patel (Product)

[00:00:05] Aisha: Hi everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood. Diego is our solutions engineer. 
[00:00:12] Rachel: Hi, Rachel here. We're excited, trying to move faster on adding an assistant into our video editor. 
[00:00:18] Ethan: Hey, Ethan. I'll be doing most of the integration work. 
[00:00:22] Sana: Sana here, product. We're focused on time-to-first-token and feel like PLG path would help us iterate. 
[00:00:30] Aisha: Great. High level: Redwood gives three hosting paths — hosted API for fastest TTFT, Dedicated if you need predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict residency. Today we can walk quickstart, free credits, and what a pilot looks like. 
[00:00:45] Rachel: Perfect. Our constraints: we need p95 latency under ~200ms for small edit suggestions, and we want data not to be retained for training. We also have internal infosec questions — SSO, KMS, audit logs. 
[00:01:03] Diego: Totally reasonable. Hosted can meet low-latency if you pick the right model and tuning — we do prefix caching and KV cache to reduce repeated context cost. Note: sometimes the transcript might call it KV "cash" in our notes, but yes KV cache.
[00:01:22] Ethan: When you say prefix caching, how does that behave with cached context per user? We're going to be doing a lot of small prompts and a larger persistent document. 
[00:01:31] Diego: Good question. We support per-user prefix caching for common system prompts and we keep the KV cache in memory on the serving runtime so repeated tokens are cheap. For PLG pilots we usually set a small TTL identity cache. Caching reduces per-token lat but doesn't change cold-start p95.
[00:01:48] Sana: We're also evaluating Dedicated — our expectation is occasional spikes during uploads and batch renders. Budget is tight though. What's the min commit for Dedicated? 
[00:01:58] Aisha: Dedicated is reserve-based, typically monthly committed capacity. For smaller teams we recommend hosted + credits first; you can always switch to Dedicated once you have predictable throughput. For the pilot we can offer 50k token credits to show TTFT and latency profiles. 
[00:02:15] Rachel: That sounds right. How long to go from sign-up to first request? We call it TTFT. 
[00:02:20] Aisha: From sign-up and API key to first successful token: most customers hit a prototype in under an hour, usually less. Our Quickstart guides plus SDKs make it very quick. Diego will also help with a sample integration for your upload pipeline. 
[00:02:35] Ethan: Nice. Are there SDKs for node/python? We use Node for the editor and a Python backend for orchestration. 
[00:02:41] Diego: Yes, official SDKs for Node and Python, plus curl examples. We'll share code snippets, and a sample repo.
[00:02:50] [00:03:05] Sana: On security: can you confirm hosted doesn't use our data for training and how do we control retention? 
[00:03:10] Diego: Hosted has a data controls page — by default we don't use customer prompts to train models. You can set retention policies per project; for more stringent requirements we suggest Private with customer-managed KMS. We'll share the security pack. 
[00:03:24] Rachel: For SOC2, do you have certification? Our procurement requires SOC2 type II. 
[00:03:29] Aisha: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 certified. We have the report and a compliance pack. We'll add that to the follow-up.
[00:03:36] Ethan: What about SSO — SAML or OIDC? Our infra team wants SAML 2.0. 
[00:03:41] Diego: We support SAML and OIDC for the Console and RBAC. For API keys in a PLG flow, teams often issue scoped keys to devs while SSO governs the Console.
[00:03:52] [00:04:20] Rachel: Ok on pricing — ballpark cost to scale to 100k monthly active users? I know it's hard to say, but any unit economics we can use. 
[00:04:28] Aisha: Unit numbers depend on prompt length and model. For a short edit suggestion prompt average ~120 tokens in / 150 out, we estimate per-1k-token costs and can model it in a spreadsheet. For the pilot we'll give numbers for a couple model variants and a suggested quantization config if you care about cost vs quality.
[00:04:47] Ethan: Quantization — do you prescriptive recommend 4-bit or 8-bit for these models? We don't want hallucinations to spike. 
[00:04:55] Diego: For many open models 4-bit QAT profiles give big cost wins and with Redwood Optimize suggestions we tune them per workload. If your quality bar is high, we can recommend mixed precision or 8-bit as a safe starting point. 
[00:05:10] Sana: Is there a way to route to cheaper model variants for non-critical flows? Like background autosuggestions using cheaper quantized models. 
[00:05:16] Aisha: Yes — smart routing policy. You can route by latency or cost. For critical paths hit low-latency variants, for background generate use quantized cheaper models. That routing is configurable in Console or via API.
[00:05:28] [00:06:00] Rachel: Benchmarks — can you run a small benchmark that mirrors our expected qps? We might want to see tail latency under load. 
[00:06:07] Diego: Absolutely. For the pilot Diego: we'll run a benchmark with your sample payloads, look at p50/p95/p99, and also measure throughput per GPU for the selected model. We'll need sample payloads and a target qps.
[00:06:22] Rachel: We'll provide payloads. Our expected peak burst is ~80 qps for short bursts. Sustained ~10 qps. 
[00:06:30] Diego: That helps — for 80 qps bursts hosted nodes with autoscaling can handle it, but if bursts are sustained we'd discuss Dedicated. We'll simulate with 100 concurrent connections.
[00:06:41] Ethan: What about private deployment? Air-gapped/on-prem— how much lead time and what's the typical package? 
[00:06:48] Aisha: Private deployments require coordination: control plane can be customer-managed, KMS integrations, and optionally an on-prem runtime. Typical lead time a few weeks to a couple months depending on procurement. For now host + pilot is the fastest path.
[00:07:02] Sana: Procurement also asked about audit logs for each token call — is there per-request tracing? 
[00:07:09] Diego: We capture request-level traces and store audit logs; retention policies configurable. We can stream logs to your customer's SIEM or S3 for long-term retention.
[00:07:20] [00:08:00] Aisha: Ok, let's outline a minimal pilot: 2-week PLG pilot, 50k token credits, Redwood sets up a sample repo and benchmark run. Success criteria: p95 < 200ms for 90% of requests in simulated traffic and quality parity above 90% for a set of eval prompts. 
[00:08:15] Rachel: That success criteria sounds reasonable. Also want the guarantee that data used in pilot won't be used for training. 
[00:08:22] Diego: Confirmed — opt-out of training for pilot, documented in the security pack.
[00:08:30] Ethan: Regarding SDK integration: can you show streaming responses? We need partial suggestions while user drags timeline. 
[00:08:36] Diego: Yes streaming is supported; we have WebSocket and SSE examples. For low-latency partial responses, you'll want to tune chunk sizes and streaming thresholds. We'll send a sample with Node SSE example.
[00:08:47] Sana: Any rate limits in the quickstart? We don't want early throttling to break our UX. 
[00:08:53] Aisha: Self-serve accounts get conservative default quotas to prevent abuse; we can bump quotas for pilot. We'll set them to match your expected qps during the pilot window.
[00:09:05] [00:10:00] Rachel: Are there any gotchas for multipart uploads? We push video metadata and thumbnails along with prompts. 
[00:10:07] Diego: Prompts with multi-part should be fine but we recommend referencing large artifacts by URL rather than embedding them. For throughput put the heavy binary data in your storage and pass a reference in the prompt.
[00:10:18] Ethan: Regarding fallbacks — if Redwood hosted has an outage, what's the recommended fallback pattern? 
[00:10:24] Aisha: Multi-region and model fallbacks. You can set an autofailover to a cheaper compatible model or a different region. Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime. Hosted has built-in redundancy and fallbacks.
[00:10:36] Rachel: For compliance, does Redwood support customer-managed keys? 
[00:10:41] Diego: Yes for Private and Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations; hosted has options for dedicated key wrapping via partner KMS for enterprise.
[00:10:52] [00:12:00] Sana: Ok, what's the timeline if we start the pilot next week? 
[00:12:06] Aisha: If you sign the quick pilot agreement early next week we can provision credits and a sandbox project same day, Diego can run the benchmark by mid-week. So end-to-end about 7–10 days to complete initial runs. 
[00:12:19] Rachel: Great. We'll discuss internally and share payloads.
[00:12:25] Ethan: Curious — do you surface token-level cost in Console so product can see spend per route? 
[00:12:30] Diego: Yes the Console has token-level breakdowns per API key/route, latency heatmaps, and per-route cost. Good for evaluating which prompts are expensive.
[00:12:41] [00:15:00] Aisha: Quick note on model selection — we have Redwood-verified model profiles in the catalog with sample latencies and cost estimates. For video-UX short prompts we usually suggest a mid-sized open model with a tuned quantization profile for cost.
[00:15:13] Ethan: If we need lower hallucination rate, can we do reranking?
[00:15:18] Diego: Yes reranking + small supervised scorer works well. We also support function-calling style structured outputs to help enforce schema.
[00:15:28] Rachel: Fantastic. Any blockers from your side?
[00:15:32] Diego: None. We just need your sample payloads and a primary contact for the pilot instrumentation.
[00:15:40] Sana: We'll assign Ethan as contact.
[00:15:43] Ethan: Happy to.
[00:15:46] [00:20:00] Aisha: I'll recap: Redwood to send pilot credits & quickstart repo, Diego to share benchmark template & streaming sample, Pinebay to provide payloads and confirm sign-off by Monday. After the pilot run we'll review p95/p99 and decide hosting strategy (stay hosted or move to Dedicated).
[00:20:20] Rachel: Sounds good. A couple quick clarifying Qs — can we have sub-accounts for different product teams? 
[00:20:26] Diego: Yes multi-tenancy via projects and scoped API keys is supported, with RBAC in Console.
[00:20:34] Sana: And are logs exportable to our S3? 
[00:20:37] Diego: Yes log export to S3 and SIEM is supported.
[00:20:42] [00:25:00] Ethan: One more, latency budgeting in the editor — what are typical cold-start latencies for the KV cache? 
[00:25:07] Diego: Cold-starts depend on model and sequence length; for small models cold-start p95 might be 200–350ms, warmed with cache we're often sub-100ms p95. That's why initial pilot benchmarks are important.
[00:25:20] Rachel: Ok that maps to our expectations. 
[00:25:24] Aisha: Anything else before we wrap?
[00:25:28] Sana: Can you include a small checklist for our security team in the follow-up? 
[00:25:31] Aisha: Yes, we'll include SOC2 report, SAML config doc, KMS options, and data retention controls.
[00:25:40] [00:30:00] Rachel: Timing wise, procurement will want pricing numbers. If pilot shows good perf we'll be ready to discuss a 6–12 month reserved plan. 
[00:30:07] Aisha: Understood. We'll include a conservative forecast model in pricing sheet.
[00:30:14] Ethan: Any notable competitor differences we should be aware of in terms of observability? 
[00:30:19] Diego: Compared to others we emphasize token-level cost breakdown, per-route tracing, and a clear quantization recommendation engine. But some competitors may have slightly lower per-token list price on certain models; our bet is on predictable serving economics and tooling.
[00:30:38] [00:34:00] Sana: Ok let's lock the next meeting — benchmark review with Diego on Thursday at 10am PT? 
[00:34:08] Aisha: Thursday 10am PT works, I'll send calendar invite.
[00:34:13] Rachel: Confirmed. 
[00:34:16] Ethan: Thanks all. 
[00:34:20] Aisha: Thanks everyone. Follow-up items out by end of day Monday.
[00:34:25] [End of recording]
